evidence.excerpt: 重庆大学图书馆按校区和学科布局设立 3 个分馆，包括 A 校区理工图书馆（含声音图书馆），B 校区建筑图书馆，虎溪校区虎溪图书馆（含 4 个舍区书屋、理学分馆、方志图书馆、科幻图书馆），还与学院合作建设有博雅分馆、新闻分馆。馆舍总面积达 59362 平方米，阅览座位 5481 个。图书馆专业馆员 99 名，设综合办公室、学科服务办公室、资源建设部、网络服务部、情报服务部、特藏部、文化育人中心、理工图书馆、建筑图 书馆、虎溪图书馆共 10 个部门，为读者提供全方位的文献服务。馆藏资源丰富，实体馆藏达 517.37 万册，数字馆藏 1424.83 万册 / 件。图书馆有线网络万兆骨干，千兆到桌面，全馆实现无线网覆盖。图书馆拥 有 21 台物理服务器和 381TB 的存储空间，为“双一流”建设、教学科研与拔尖创新人才培养提供了强有力的文献资源保障。 重庆大学图书馆致力于推动学校及社会创新发展提供信息研究及 分析服务，设有教育部首批科技查新站，2018 年获批首批高校国家知识产权信息服务中心，2020 年获批世界知识产权组织在华设立的技术与创新支持中心（TISC）。图书馆积极参与国家、省市级文献资源保 障体系建设，是教育部文献保障体系 CALIS 省级服务中心、重庆市大学联盟资源平台共建单位、重庆市高校图工委常设秘书处所在单位。 重庆大学图书馆馆庆日为每年 10 月 12 日。虚拟形象为书妹儿。吉祥物为学霸雁。 A校区理工图书馆

evidence.excerpt: ion. 4. Tutors (Buddy System) All NUPACE students are eligible to receive the services of a tutor, a fellow student majoring in a similar field of study. Tutoring assistance is available for fifteen hours per semester, and tutors' responsibilities may include, 1) assistance with university paperwork and official procedures after arrival, 2) advice on the use of university facilities related to aca-demic studies, 3) assistance and guidance with regard to lectures, research, experiments, course preparation, and reports, 4) Japanese language and conversation support, and 5) the introduc-tion of Japanese culture and customs. 5. Extracurricular Activities Nagoya University has a wide range of cultural and sports clubs, officially boasting fifty-three of the former and forty-three of the latter, with a total membership of 3,500 students. These provide international and Japanese students with an excellent opportunity to mix, and thus participate in a cross-cultural learning experience. 6. Cross-cultural Exchange Groups There is a host of volunteer groups involved with international students both amongst the campus community and outside. These depend for their existence on the co-operation of each and every international student, and greatly contribute to enriching student and community life. Information on these groups will be made available at the general orientation for NUPACE students. 7. Exchange Activities outside Nagoya During the spring, summer and winter vacations, various associations host home-visits or camping activities. If taken advantage of properly, these present an excellent opportunity to deepen one’s knowledge of Japan at comparatively little cost. All Tohoku University students and faculty members can take the bus to move between campuses to attend lectures, talks, meetings, student activities, etc. On top of that, students can also use the Aobayama Shuttle Bus to commute from their homes to the university. There are 2 types of shuttle services available : Tohoku University Campus Bus (runs between TU campuses) Aobayama Shuttle Bus (departs from Aobayama station and stops at points around Aobayama campus) Please be advised that although the Aobayama Shuttle Bus can be used by students to commute between their homes and the university, researchers and faculty members are only allowed to use the bus to travel between campuses, and not to commute to the university from their place of residence. IC Card IC Card (icsca) With the IC card “icsca”, you can use the bus and subway systems smoothly. Add funds and use it to travel around Sendai. When buying a new icsca card, you must pay a deposit of JPY 500. This deposit can be refunded if you no longer need your icsca card and return it. Registered icsca cards can be used as bus commuter passes, subway-bus commuter passes, or the Gakuto Sendai Free Pass. Where to buy In addition to ticket vending machines at subway stations, you can buy them on buses, at bus stations, and at some Miyagi Co-op stores. Cards sold on buses and at Miyagi Co-op stores are unregistered icsca cards (JPY 2,000). Click here for the details. Where to add funds You can add funds to your card at subway station ticket machines, bus stations, some Miyagi Co-op stores, and on buses. unrequested_discovered_links.label:
Program Overview Exchange Student Program  
International students can take courses at Kyung Hee University either in Korean or English as an exchange student for up to one academic year.
 International students from partner institutions are eligible for our exchange program and their tuition at KHU is waived under the bilateral agreements.
 KHU currently offers over 30% of courses in English in a variety of fields including Management, Hotel and Tourism Management.



 

Visiting Student Program  
Visiting Student Program allows you to spend 1-2 semesters at Kyung Hee University.
 We eagerly provide you one of the best international study options in Korea. 


Eligibility Academic Requirements - Must be an currently enrolled undergraduate student at a four-year university
- Must have an overall GPA of 2.5 out of 4.0 or above
- Must have more than one semester remaining at home university after the completion of visiting program Language Proficiency - TOPIK Level 3 or above (Level 4 for College of Business Administration) - in case of taking courses conducted in Korean
   ** Required minimum will be raised to TOPIK Level 5 or above, starting from Fall 2025** - TOEFL iBT 82 / IELTS 6.5 or higher recommended- in case of taking courses conducted in English
 * If applying to study in his/her native language, a proof of language proficiency is not required

Tuition and Fee
Students are responsible for tuition and living expenses in Korea
Tuition Fee: KRW 6,536,000 / Semester (Subject to change and may vary depending on the program)

Procedure
1. Apply to the exchange student program at your university's International Office : We require email  nomination from your university.
* For Visiting Students Program : Please email us to express your interest in participating in the visiting student program by (Spring semester) October 20 / (Fall semester) April 20. 
We require a confirmation email from your home university that you are eligible to participate in the visiting program and transfer your credits back to your home university.
2. Submit all Required documents to Kyung Hee University via online (Some may require post mail submission)
   - Complete list of documents required will be announced later to participating students 3. Visa Issuance
 4. Book Flight Ticket
 5. Course Registration
6. Dormitory Check-in
7. Study at KHU with 2 exams(Midterm/Final)
8. Receive transcript of record


THE ABOVE IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE
International Exchange Office of International Affairs

The review may take up to one week. Students can find the link under “Your Application Status.” 1. PDF version of Online Exchange Application form: https://wis.hufs.ac.kr/src08/jsp/fexchange/index.html 2. 1 brief essay of personal history and plan of study 3. 1 copy of academic transcript 4. 1 certificate of current enrollment at home university ( students joining with a passport from a non-OECD country must have an apostille or Korean embassy/consulate authentication on the certificate ) 5. 1 copy of evidence of proficiency in English language or reference letter 6. 1 copy of the information page of passport 7. Dorm application form (if applying for Dorm) 8. Health documents for dormitory applicants (requested after dormitory assignment) 9. 1 photo (3X4cm) with white background color (in JPG file) 10. 1 copy of financial affidavit/statement. It will be requested after the application period has ended via a separate form. - Students joining with a passport from an OECD country should submit the HUFS Financial Affidavit form ONLY. This form will be provided for students later on. We do not require students to submit proof of a bank account, statement or letter. - Students joining us with a non-OECD passport must submit 1) HUFS Financial Certification form (will be provided for students later on), AND 2) Proof of financial amount, either a bank statement or letter. Please check our online factsheet for more information: www.hufs.ac.kr/HUFSfactsheet 11. 1 page min. of study essay for Intensive Korean Program applicants

evidence.excerpt: ou can get to the university: By tramway : the B line runs from 5am to midnight on weekdays (and up to 1am on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays), with trams running every 10 minutes on average. The university is located right next to the "Montaigne-Montesquieu" tram stop. By bus : you can get from the train station to Bordeaux Montaigne University on lines 31 and 35 . The night line, TBNight , also serves the campus (Talence, Pessac and Gradignan) on Thursday, Friday and Saturday from 1.30am to 6.30am. By bike : the TBM network provides more than 2,000 self-service bikes, including 1,000 electric ones. You can also access TBM " vélo'c " bike loan, hire and parking service. By car : you can check the rules for the use of foreign licences at https://www.service-public.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/N19126?lang=en Useful information At Étu’Recup ’s « Maison du vélo », you can buy refurbished bikes at very reasonable prices. The association also offers bike repair workshops, where volunteers and technicians are on hand to help all participants with their diagnostics and repairs. There, you can also find low-cost second-hand parts. 5 intercity bus routes serve the Talence campus: lines 406, 502, 503, 504 and 505. Bus line 602 (Hôpital Pellegrin - Pieces de Choisy) stops at Bordeaux Montaigne campus (Unitec). Depending on your income or circumstances, you may be eligible for the TBM Solidarity Fare scheme, which offers significant discounts (or even free travel) on your travel pass. evidence.excerpt: Comment se rendre à l’université ? L’Université Bordeaux Montaigne est située sur le campus Pessac-Talence-Gradignan, à 6 km du centre-ville de Bordeaux. Vous pouvez vous rendre à l’université : En tram : la ligne B circule de 5h du matin à minuit en semaine (ou jusqu'à 1h les jeudi, vendredi et samedi). Le tramway passe en moyenne toutes les 10 minutes. En bus : vous pouvez vous rendre à l'Université Bordeaux Montaigne grâce aux lignes 31 et 35 (depuis la gare). La ligne de nuit, TBNight , dessert également le campus (Talence, Pessac et Gradignan) de jeudi à samedi soir de 1h30 du matin à 6h30. Tram (1st tram network in France), bus , bicycle (1st bike paths network in France), car-sharing or walking ... There are various possibilites for you to get around Strasbourg. Getting around in Strasbourg is easy because the city has a very good transportation system. Trams and buses spread over more than 77 kilometers. The tram system in Strasbourg is the longest one in France, and it even goes into Germany, all the way to Kehl. Around 375,000 people use the tram to get around anyway. There are also 39 different bus lines in the city, including 3 that run at night, 1 shuttle service, 5 taxibuses, and a service you can book in advance if you need it. evidence.excerpt: off-campus buildings nearby. Students walk and ride their bikes between dorms and classes. Those living off-campus ride their bikes or take city buses to class. Bike If you like cyclying, you'll love Pardubice! The city is flat and bike-friendly with a network of cycling paths. Biking is the fastest way to get around the city. Bus The city has an exceptional public bus service. Buses go frequently and reach all points in the city. Several buses stop at, or just next to, the University campus. These bus stop names are "Polabiny, Hradecká" (buses 3, 7, 17, 33) and "Univerzita" (buses 10, 16). Pardubice city bus schedules are online at www.dpmp.cz . evidence.excerpt: By train The Czech Republic has an extensive railway network, operated by four major railway companies: České dráhy (ČD, Czech Railways), RegioJet , LEO Express , and Arriva . The timetables and connections are changing approximately once per year. Due to that, we recommend checking the connections at the websites of the mentioned railway companies. Zlín itself has several train stations even though they are all quite small. The main train station is called Zlín – Střed and it has only one direct train from Prague ( Zlínský expres ). However, the neighbouring town Otrokovice is placed on the main train corridor. Due to that, it is possible to get directly from Otrokovice to five European capitals (Bratislava, Budapest, Prague, Vienna, and Warsaw). So, it is possible to search for the connections to Otrokovice and then use the public transportation working between Zlín and Otrokovice.
